captured_client_source.meaning: Captured source defaults are longer than the observed failure. The startup model_kwargs contain no explicit request-timeout override. No active process environment was inspected, so defaults are not asserted to be the effective live timeout.

conclusions: No demonstrated client-side fix or alternate supported route preserves the current task/model/effort/max_tokens through this failure.

The roughly 290.5-second EOF does not distinguish absolute function lifetime, upstream timeout, idle timeout, buffering, or another remote/network close. Long-run wire/SSE last-byte telemetry and deployment logs are missing.
Increasing a local read timeout cannot make a remotely ended response continue. Streaming is already enabled and has not yet demonstrated relief for long requests.
Owner-side maxDuration/upstream timeout adjustment or an owner-supported equivalent long-running route could preserve the benchmark request; neither is an available proven local setting.

http2_untested.reason: Captured HTTPX defaults HTTP/1.1 and h2 is absent. A future HTTP/2 experiment needs dependency/transport changes and separate validation. PING can address some idle-connection paths, but cannot extend a function/upstream absolute deadline or restore an ended stream.

observed.timestamp_provenance: UTC conversion of query number 18 epochs in the bound long-request-failure-001.json. long_request_observed_at is the later audit observation time, not the request time. instrumented_event_types describes the full saved event snapshot, including completed earlier queries; failed_request_event_types describes only request 18.

owner_checks: Correlate the saved trial/request timestamps with function/CDN/upstream logs and identify which layer closes the response.
Inspect deployed runtime, plan, Fluid setting, per-route maxDuration, and upstream request/read/abort timeout.
If idle or buffering is responsible, verify timely end-to-end SSE flush/heartbeat forwarding; if absolute duration is responsible, use an eligible longer-duration runtime or supported route.
Provide a supported route/setting preserving the exact model, max effort, adaptive thinking, 64000 max_tokens and original task budgets; do not substitute a cheaper request configuration.

primary_documentation.deployment_applicability: Unknown: runtime, plan, Fluid setting, maxDuration, upstream fetch deadline and proxy buffering are not available in saved evidence.
findings: Function duration includes time waiting for streamed responses; exceeding it terminates the invocation.
Fluid default is 300 seconds; Pro/Enterprise generally available maximum is 800 seconds; supported runtimes can opt into 1800 seconds beta per function, subject to documented exclusions.
Settings belong in deployment function code/vercel.json or owner dashboard; client request parameters do not set deployment maxDuration.
For eligible long handlers, HTTP/2 has connection-level PING support; HTTP/1.1 idle connections may need streamed progress/heartbeat data.
Confirms owner-configured extended durations for supported Fluid Node.js/Python deployments.
